pages.title: Paid Men
pages.text: I hired four men to go down with me. Swords, rope, lamps, and my coin up front, because they asked for it up front.$(br2)I was looking for what cursed the land above my hut. Fields that would not take seed. Wells gone bitter. Everyone blamed the weather. I knew it came from under us.

pages.title: The Fall
pages.text: In the deep dark the floor opened under me. I fell into a city nobody built in our age. When I could stand I heard them above, arguing. Then I heard them leave. They had my pay already. They did not even drop a rope.$(br2)I remember their names. I write them nowhere, so I cannot burn the page in a temper.

pages.title: The City
pages.text: The city is stone, clean and cold, and the sculk grows over it like moss on a grave. Something walks its halls and hunts by sound. I learned to walk on wool and to breathe slowly. I learned that the sculk listens.$(br2)In the middle of the city stands a great frame. Its portal is dead.

pages.title: The Eye
pages.text: Under the frame I found a rift. A tear in the air, violet at the lips, black inside. In the black, an eye. It looked at me as if it had waited.$(br2)Its words came behind my own eyes. Where to step. When to hold my breath. How the old builders made their stone listen. I do not know what it is. It kept me alive.

pages.title: How to Read It
pages.text: This is my grimoire, kept in the dark. I write what I built and what it cost me. The numbers are true. I counted them when I had nothing to do but count.$(br2)The later pages are not as calm as these. Forgive the hand. You will see why.
